parameters.content:
## Invoice Automation - Stock Template

Two triggers feed the same pipeline:
- Manual Trigger + "Sample Job Data" -> click-to-test in the n8n editor.
- Webhook "Job Completion Input" -> POST real (or test) job-completion JSON here; also what a real job-management system would call.

Flow: validate -> Client Config -> normalize paymentMethod -> branding/discount/payment options -> send-window check (queues via a Wait node if outside window) -> resolve Xero contact (search by AccountNumber == internal customerId; create if not found) -> duplicate check (by Reference on the invoice) -> branch on paymentMethod:
- "Send Invoice" (or blank/unrecognized, defaulted with a warning) -> create Xero DRAFT invoice -> Resend confirmation email if we have one. Eligible for Collections/Reminders as normal.
- "Paid Cash" -> create Xero AUTHORISED invoice -> record a full Xero Payment against it (xeroCashAccountCode) -> no email. AmountDue becomes 0, so Collections/Reminders' own where-filter (AmountDue>0) naturally excludes it - nothing else needed to keep it out of the chase.

Webhook responds with whatever the final node in the branch that fired produced (responseMode: lastNode), so POSTing test payloads is a full round-trip test.

parameters.jsCode:
return [{ json: {
  jobId: 'JOB-1001',
  customerId: 'CUST-001',
  customerName: 'Jane Doe',
  customerEmail: 'jane@example.com',
  jobDescription: 'Boiler service and safety check',
  jobValue: 250.00,
  paymentMethod: 'Send Invoice',
  milestoneNumber: null,
  milestoneLabel: null,
  jobCompletedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
} }];

const body = $json.body || {};
return [{ json: { ...body } }];

nodes.name: Normalize Payment Method
nodes.notes: Blank/unrecognized paymentMethod defaults to 'Send Invoice' behavior (not a validation failure - the job still gets invoiced) but is flagged via paymentMethodWarning, which flows through to the final result so it's visible in the response/execution, plus a best-effort this.logger.warn() call. Parameter-shape flag: this.logger's availability inside a Code node is unverified on this n8n version - wrapped in try/catch so it can never break the run either way.

nodes.name: Check Customer Discount
nodes.notes: Raw Sheets REST API call (values.get), not the native Google Sheets node - that node's column-mapping behavior proved unreliable in live testing (silently merged unrelated fields into written rows), while this raw pattern is the same proven-working approach used for Xero throughout this project. Reads the whole Discounts tab (expected small); matched against customerId in the next node.

nodes.name: Match Customer Discount
nodes.notes: Falls back to Client Config's flat discountPercent if the customer has no row in the Discounts tab. discountSource is just for visibility/debugging - not used downstream.

parameters.jsCode:
const d = $input.item.json;
return [{ json: { ...d, queueStatus: 'queued_outside_send_window', queuedUntil: d.resumeAt } }];

nodes.name: Xero - Search Contact
nodes.notes: Searches by Name, not AccountNumber/customerId - see 'Contact Search Result' for the email/phone disambiguation this requires. Xero itself enforces unique contact Names within an org (a same-Name POST updates the existing contact rather than creating a second one), which is exactly why a raw name match on its own is not a safe signal that it's the same person.

nodes.name: Contact Search Result
nodes.notes: Name match alone is not enough to reuse a contact: also requires the existing Xero contact's stored email OR phone to match the current job's customerEmail/customerPhone. A name match with no email/phone overlap (or the stored contact has neither on file) is flagged via nameMatchedDifferentPerson and falls through to contact creation, treating it as a different person.

parameters.jsCode:
const d = $input.item.json;
return [{ json: { ...d, resolvedContactId: d.existingContactId, contactResolution: 'existing' } }];

nodes.name: Xero - Create Contact
nodes.notes: Xero enforces unique contact Names within an org - POSTing an unmodified Name that already exists updates that existing contact instead of creating a second one (confirmed via live testing). When nameMatchedDifferentPerson is true (same name, no email/phone overlap - a different person), the Name is suffixed with the internal customerId so Xero actually creates a separate contact instead of silently merging into the wrong person's record. This is a visible, deliberate tradeoff: that customer's name shows with the suffix on this invoice/contact record.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ Contacts: [{ Name: $json.nameMatchedDifferentPerson ? `${$json.customerName} (${$json.customerId})` : $json.customerName, EmailAddress: $json.customerEmail || undefined, Phones: $json.customerPhone ? [{ PhoneType: 'DEFAULT', PhoneNumber: $json.customerPhone }] : undefined, AccountNumber: $json.customerId }] }) }}

nodes.name: Is Paid Cash?
nodes.notes: Both branches share every node up to here (discount, branding, send-window, duplicate check by Reference, contact resolution) - only invoice creation and what happens after it differ. TRUE (Paid Cash): creates an AUTHORISED invoice + a Payment against xeroCashAccountCode, no email. FALSE (Send Invoice, or blank/unrecognized defaulted by 'Normalize Payment Method'): the original unchanged flow - DRAFT invoice (per invoiceStatus config) + Resend confirmation.

nodes.name: Xero - Create Invoice (Cash Sale)
nodes.notes: Status is hardcoded to AUTHORISED here regardless of the invoiceStatus Client Config value - a Payment cannot be applied to a DRAFT invoice in Xero. DueDate is today (already paid), not invoiceDueDays out.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ Invoices: [{ Type: 'ACCREC', Contact: { ContactID: $json.resolvedContactId }, LineAmountTypes: $json.invoiceLineAmountType || 'Inclusive', LineItems: $json.xeroLineItems, Reference: $json.invoiceReference + ' | PAID CASH - approve and mark paid in Xero', Status: 'DRAFT', DueDate: new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10) }] }) }}

nodes.name: Xero - Create Payment
nodes.notes: Parameter-shape flag: this is a new Xero object type for this project (Payments, not Invoices/Contacts/History). Account.Code must be a real BANK or CASH type account in the client's chart of accounts (xeroCashAccountCode in Client Config) - posting against a REVENUE account (like xeroSalesAccountCode) is rejected by Xero. Unverified against real client chart-of-accounts data.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ Invoice: { InvoiceID: $json.invoiceId }, Account: { Code: $json.xeroCashAccountCode }, Date: new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10), Amount: $json.lineAmount }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ Invoices: [{ Type: 'ACCREC', Contact: { ContactID: $json.resolvedContactId }, LineAmountTypes: $json.invoiceLineAmountType || 'Inclusive', LineItems: $json.xeroLineItems, Reference: $json.invoiceReference, Status: 'DRAFT', DueDate: new Date(Date.now() + (Number($json.invoiceDueDays) || 14) * 86400000).toISOString().slice(0,10) }] }) }}

nodes.name: Send Confirmation Email (Resend)
nodes.notes: Resend API - POST /emails. Uses the 'Header Auth account 2' credential (header Authorization: Bearer <resend-api-key>).

parameters.jsCode:
const d = $('Parse Invoice Result').item.json;
return [{ json: {
  status: 'success',
  jobId: d.jobId,
  paymentMethod: 'send_invoice',
  invoiceId: d.invoiceId,
  invoiceNumber: d.invoiceNumber,
  invoiceReference: d.invoiceReference,
  contactId: d.resolvedContactId,
  contactResolution: d.contactResolution,
  amount: d.lineAmount,
  emailSent: true,
  paymentMethodWarning: d.paymentMethodWarning || null,
} }];

const d = $input.item.json;
return [{ json: {
  status: 'success',
  jobId: d.jobId,
  paymentMethod: 'send_invoice',
  invoiceId: d.invoiceId,
  invoiceNumber: d.invoiceNumber,
  invoiceReference: d.invoiceReference,
  contactId: d.resolvedContactId,
  contactResolution: d.contactResolution,
  amount: d.lineAmount,
  emailSent: false,
  emailSkippedReason: 'missing_customer_email',
  paymentMethodWarning: d.paymentMethodWarning || null,
} }];
return { json: $json.job };

const j = $('Prepare Needs Review').item.json.job;
return { json: { status: 'needs_review', reason: $('Prepare Needs Review').item.json.reason || 'Sent to Keystone Needs Review', jobId: j.jobId || null, errors: j.validationErrors } };
return { json: $('Prepare Agent Log').item.json.result };
